text: Several ores of copper contain both copper(II) carbonate and copper(II) hydroxide. This combination
is called basic copper(II) carbonate. You will determine the composition of an ore of copper by
reacting it with an excess of acid and collecting the gas evolved.
CuCO (s) + H SO (aq) CuSO (aq) + H O(l) + CO (g)
FA 1 is a sample of basic copper(II) carbonate.
FA 2 is dilute sulfuric acid, H SO .
The formula of basic copper(II) carbonate, FA 1, can be written as xCuCO •yCu(OH) .
